chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Abu Ayoub al-Madainy, from Suleyman al-Ja'fary, from al-Rida, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
Grey hair in the front part of the head is a blessing, and in the two sides is generosity, and in the top is courage, and in the back is inauspiciousness.

key_terms.مُقَدَّمِ الرَّأْسِ: The front part of the head

ai.seo_question: What do different locations of grey hair signify in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him), transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni in *Al-Kafi*, the physical manifestation of aging is interpreted through a lens of spiritual and character symbolism, reflecting the Shia tradition of finding deeper meanings in bodily signs. While grey hair at the front signifies blessing (yumn) and on the temples indicates generosity, its presence at the nape (qafa) is viewed as inauspicious, a nuance often discussed by scholars regarding the balance between natural signs and divine decree. This interpretation aligns with the broader Islamic view that physical attributes can serve as indicators of inner qualities, though they are not deterministic.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Abu Ayoub Al Madainy, from Suleyman Al Ja’fary, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> forefathers<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
The grey hair in the front part of the head is a Blessing, and in the two sides is generosity, and in the top is courage, and in the back is inauspiciousness’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah fn abu Ayyub al-Madiniy from Sulayman al-Ja‘fariy who has said the following: “Al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has narrated from his ancestors saying, ‘
Gray in front of the head is good fortune, on the sides is generosity, on top of the head is courage, and at the back is misfortune.’”
